annual.label: Avg yearly maintenance (KBB 5-year estimate via Recharged, at 15,000 mi/yr)

maint.job: Front brake pads and rotors (one axle)
maint.every: Pads often last 50,000–80,000 miles thanks to regenerative braking; rotors around 70,000–90,000
maint.note: Pads alone (no rotors) run about $250–$750 per axle. New pad wear sensors are usually needed.

maint.job: Rear brake pads and rotors (one axle)
maint.every: Pads often last 50,000–80,000 miles; inspect at each annual service
maint.note: Light use can let rotors rust, which is a common reason to replace them early on EVs.

maint.every: About every 4–6 years, if it tests weak
maint.note: This is the small 12-volt battery that runs the car's computers, not the high-voltage drive battery. It must be registered to the car after replacement.

maint.job: Battery and drive-unit coolant check or service
maint.every: About every 4–6 years, depending on model year
maint.note: Brake fluid also needs changing about every 2 years ($120–$220).
